topic: Lambert-Arvo closed-form polygonal area-light contour integral vs center-point 1/r2 blowout rig
topic_zh: Lambert-Arvo 斯托克斯多边形面光源边界环路闭式积分对比中心点光源平方反比过曝
scope: Deterministic Lambert (1760) / Arvo (1995) / Heitz et al. (2016) closed-form boundary edge-contour integration versus naive center-point inverse-square approximation across 17 receiver elevations under a 4m x 4m area light. No neural relighting execution.

robustness.name: Sampled 17 receiver distances (0.15m..2.55m) preserve unit hemisphere irradiance conservation E <= 1.0

good_fit: Real-time architectural windows, virtual-production LED softbox panels, emissive signage, and Linearly Transformed Cosines (LTC) polygonal area lights
Explaining why replacing an area panel with a center point light creates an unphysical 1/r^2 singularity when h < panel width
Reducing a 2D surface integral over an M-gon to an exact noise-free 1D sum over its M boundary edges via Stokes' theorem
Evaluating edge arc-length and normal projection directly from u_k x u_{k+1} without per-edge Gram-Schmidt tangent orthogonalization
not_for: Textured area lights with high-frequency video content without pre-filtered mipmap lookup over the polygon footprint
Contact-hardening area-light shadows (umbrae/penumbrae) without an accompanying blocker search or ray-traced visibility pass
Single-image diffusion portrait relighting models (IC-Light / DiLightNet)
Infinitely distant directional sunlight where solid angle is small and constant across the scene
